title: How Do Wrinkly Fingers Grab 12% Faster? 🖐️
description:
Why do your fingers wrinkle in water? It isn't soggy skin: your nerves wrinkle your fingertips on purpose, and wrinkly fingers move wet objects 12% faster.

topic: Why do your fingers wrinkle in water? (nerves constrict blood vessels; wrinkles help grip wet objects)
script:
Stop blaming the water.
Your nerves wrinkle your fingers on purpose.
For years, people blamed water soaking into the skin.
But since the 1930s, doctors noticed something odd.
If a finger's nerves are damaged,
that finger stays perfectly smooth.
So it isn't the water. It's you.
After a long soak, your nervous system squeezes
the tiny blood vessels under your fingertips.
The pads shrink, and the skin folds into ridges,
like the treads on a rain tire.
In 2013, scientists tested it with marbles.
With wrinkly fingers, people moved wet marbles
twelve percent faster.
Dry marbles? No difference at all.
So, are those soggy fingers,
or your built-in rain tires?
key_facts: Finger wrinkling in water is an involuntary response of the autonomic nervous system, caused by blood vessels constricting below the skin (Nature news, 2013; Newcastle University)
Researchers have known since the 1930s that wrinkling does not happen when the nerves in the fingers are damaged (Nature news, 2013)
Kareklas, Nettle & Smulders (Newcastle, Biology Letters 2013): after 30 min in warm water, people moved wet marbles 12% faster with wrinkled fingers
Wrinkles made no difference for moving dry objects
Wrinkles are thought to channel water away like treads on a rain tire
